item.title: You Can Finally See When a Gambit Fires: The 1.5.4b Visual Effects Pass
item.description:
MID GAME

Eight Gambits got their missing visual effects on 30 September 2026. Nothing about their numbers changed, but a Gambit you can see firing is a Gambit you can actually debug in the middle of a run.

The official ART line names all eight: Dainsleif’s, King XI’s, Resurrection Stone’s, Anna’s Family’s, Zen’s, Jockey’s, Princess’s and Warlock’s Gambit.

item.title: Enemies Clear Their Old Tiles Reliably in 1.5.6: What No Longer Lingers Between Fights
item.description:
MID GAME

A leftover tile you cannot interact with is worse than no tile at all, because you plan around it. The 1.5.6 post spends four words on this: enemies clear their old tile reliably.

It is a cleanup fix. The rule did not change, the visual did. Old enemy tiles now clear when they should, so the board in front of you is the board you are actually playing on.

item.title: Magic Tiles Strain Now Puts Phantom Tiles in the Starting Pool (1.5.6)
item.description:
MID GAME

The entire 1.5.6 line about Magic Tiles is one sentence: phantom tiles are now in the pool of tiles available at the start. If you were treating your opening board as a fixed set of possibilities, that sentence changes what you check in staging.

It is a pool change, not a new tile. The tile and its behaviour already existed. What 1.5.6 changed is that the Strain can now offer it among the tiles available when a run begins.

item.title: Quick Restart No Longer Wipes Gambit Medal Progress After 1.5.4b
item.description:
MID GAME

Losing progress is the one bug that changes how people play. If a restart looks like it wipes your medal, you stop restarting, and that is a much bigger cost than the medal itself.

1.5.4b lists it under fixes, not changes. Fixed an issue where Gambit Medal progress would reset after using Quick Restart. The progress was always supposed to stay.

item.title: Valhalla's Gambit Is $8 Now: Buy, Skip, or Wait for the Next Shop
item.description:
MID GAME

The price moved from $10 to $8 and the temptation is to call that a buff. It is not. It is a discount, and the only question a discount changes is what else that money could have bought in the same shop.

**$2 is exactly one reroll.** Every shop between games offers one random piece, three random Gambits and three random tokens, with a $2 reroll. The Valhalla cut hands you back precisely one extra look.

item.title: Six Gambit Bugs Fixed in 1.5.4b: A Check-Your-Client Checklist
item.description:
MID GAME

Some bugs cost you a run. Others quietly cost you a Gambit slot. The 1.5.4b fixes are mostly the second kind, which is exactly why players kept misreading them as balance changes for a month.

Six fixes shipped on 30 September 2026. Two were visual or platform issues, four were state bugs that made a Gambit or a progress counter behave as if it were broken, because it was.

item.title: Golden Idol's Proc Rate Went From 1/3 to 1/2 in 1.5.7: What That Does to Your Build Math
item.description:
MID GAME

One number changed on 2 November 2026: Golden Idol’s Gambit now procs on 1/2 instead of 1/3. That is the whole patch line, and it is also the kind of line players consistently over-read into a damage buff.

It is a 1.5x increase in trigger frequency, not a 1.5x increase in anything else. Over six chances, the old rate expected 2 procs and the new rate expects 3. Nothing in the note changes what a proc does.

item.title: 1.5.4b Changed Two Rules, Not Twenty: The Rook-King Protection and the $2 Valhalla Cut
item.description:
MID GAME

If you skimmed the 1.5.4b notes and assumed the whole meta moved, it did not. Six lines in that post are bug fixes, two lines are design changes, and one is an art pass. Only two rules in the game actually behave differently today.

Mercenary’s Gambit now protects both pieces. The developer’s before-and-after line is exact: before, moving a ROOK ADJACENT to a KING protected it; after, moving a ROOK ADJACENT to a KING protects them both.

item.title: Gambonanza 1.4.0 Patch Breakdown: Enhanced AI, the Graveyard & Every Change That Matters
item.description:
v1.4.0 is a feature-forward update, not a balance nuke. The two headline systems are Enhanced AI Mode (a toggle for players who want conventional chess instead of rogue chaos) and The Graveyard (a PAWN-difficulty safety net that lets you buy back your last 5 lost pieces). Under the hood, Yin and Yang Gambits jumped to a 1/2 trigger, promote-into-PAWN is now real, and three Gambits got meaningful revamps. If you only change one habit after this patch, turn on Skip Animations in the new Extra settings tab.

What Landed in 1.4.0

This is every material change pulled straight from the official Steam news posts (1.4.0, plus hotfixes 1.4.0e and 1.4.0f), and what each one means for your next run.

item.title: Gambonanza 1.5.0 Patch Breakdown: UI Revamp, Steam Deck Verified & Enemy Power Feedback
item.description:
MID GAME
v1.5.0 is a polish and accessibility update, not a balance shakeup. The three things that matter: a UI and text revamp that makes the board far easier to read (mainly for Steam Deck), new feedback when an enemy power is about to trigger so you can react in time, and several achievement bug fixes. The headline is that Gambonanza is now officially Steam Deck Verified. No Gambit numbers changed, so your builds carry over untouched.
Update your client, then open Settings and confirm the Extra toggles are present. If they are missing, you are not on 1.5.x yet. The enemy power warning only appears on the current build.

What Landed in 1.5.0

This is every material change pulled straight from the official 1.5.0 Steam news post, plus the hotfixes that followed it (1.5.1, 1.5.2b, 1.5.3). If you only read one section, read the verdict above: nothing here changes your Gambit math, so your existing tier lists and build notes are still valid.

item.title: Gambonanza 1.5.1 to 1.5.3 Patch Notes Explained: Stalemate Resets the Graveyard
item.description:
MID GAME
The 1.5.x hotfix line is small but it changes three real things. Stalemate now resets the Graveyard (1.5.1). Barter’s Gambit now resets on the shop after a Graveyard (1.5.1). Key of Life’s Gambit now resets after a Stalemate (1.5.1). The rest are presentation and platform fixes, but the “Enemy Modifiers” tab is now simply called “Enemies”, which is worth knowing when you hunt for it.
Three reset rules changed in a single hotfix. Read Barter, Key of Life, and the Graveyard as one system, not three isolated notes, because they interact inside the same run.

Why a Hotfix Line Deserves Its Own Guide

Major patches get the attention, but hotfixes are where the developer quietly rebalances the rules that bite you in a run. The 1.5.1 hotfix alone touches three Gambit and system reset rules. If you play Gambit-heavy builds that lean on repeatable triggers, these are not cosmetic notes. They change how many times per run you can expect a trigger to fire.
